name: Aqara Smart Plug (US, ZNCZ12LM)

radios.note: Zigbee; it talks to an Aqara Zigbee 3.0 hub, not to Wi-Fi.

matter.note: No CSA listing found for ZNCZ12LM; the plug itself is Zigbee. Aqara's Hub M3 can expose Aqara Zigbee devices to Matter as a bridge, but no page names this plug.

apple_home.note: Aqara lists Apple HomeKit; it reaches Apple Home through an Aqara hub.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Google Assistant; works through an Aqara hub and the Aqara account link.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Amazon Alexa; works through an Aqara hub and the Aqara skill.

smartthings.note: Aqara's partnerships page lists SmartThings, but the US spec sheet and store page don't, and that partner page also shows EU ratings (10 A / 2300 W). Official sources disagree.

home_assistant.note: No official Aqara or Home Assistant page names this model. Users run Aqara Zigbee plugs through Zigbee coordinators, but that isn't documented here.

hubRequired.note: Spec sheet: hub required (Aqara Zigbee 3.0 hub). Sold without a hub.

localControl.note: We found no Aqara US page on whether it keeps working through the hub without internet.

energyMonitoring.note: Aqara says the app records the plugged-in appliance's power use on a daily and monthly basis.

maxLoadWatts.note: 1875 W, 15 A, 100-125 V AC, 60 Hz. One Aqara partnerships page shows 10 A / 2300 W, which matches the EU model, not this one.

summary: The Aqara Smart Plug for the US (ZNCZ12LM) is a Zigbee plug that needs an Aqara hub; it can't join Wi-Fi itself. Through the hub, Aqara lists Apple HomeKit, Alexa and Google Assistant, and the Aqara app tracks energy use. Aqara rates it at 15 A / 1875 W.
caveats: Needs an Aqara Zigbee hub, sold separately.
SmartThings support is unclear: Aqara's own pages disagree.
No Matter on the plug itself; a Matter bridge such as the Aqara Hub M3 is the route to Matter.
